chunks: Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Amr ibn Sa'id, from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqa, from Ammar ibn Musa, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
regarding the menstruating woman who washes herself (performs ghusl) while saffron remains on her body that the water has not removed. He said: There is no problem.

key_terms.الحائض: The menstruating woman — one who is in the state of hayd (menstruation), requiring ghusl for re-entry into worship
key_terms.الزعفران: Saffron — a prized spice and dye used cosmetically and medicinally in classical Islamic societies
key_terms.تغتسل: She performs ghusl — the full ritual bath required after menstruation, sexual intercourse, or other states of major ritual impurity
key_terms.لا بأس: There is no problem — a standard juristic formula indicating permissibility or non-liability

ai.seo_question: Does saffron remaining on the body invalidate the ghusl of a menstruating woman?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) rules that a woman performing ghusl after menstruation need not be concerned if saffron or dye on her body is not completely washed away by the water. The ruling indicates that the validity of ritual purification does not require removal of every external substance, reflecting a practical concession in Islamic jurisprudence. This question likely arose in a context where saffron was used as a cosmetic or medicinal substance by women, and the questioner sought to know whether its presence on the body during ghusl would invalidate the ritual bath.

en.hubeali: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Ahmad, from Ahmad Bin Al Hassan Bin Ali, from Amro Bin Saeed, from Musaddaq Bin Sadaqa, from Ammar Bin Musa,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> regarding the menstruating woman washing herself and upon her body is saffron, not going away with the water’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no problem’.
en.sarwar: 5. Abu Ali al-Ash’ariy has narrated from Muhammad ibn Ahmad from Ahmad ibn al-Hassan ibn Ali from ‘Amr ibn Sa‘id from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqah from ‘Ammar ibn Musa who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam,
about a woman who takes Ghusl (bath) because of Hayd (menses) and there is saffron on her body which is not removed with Ghusl (bath), has said, ‘It is not harmful.
